title: Fix delayed quota reconciliation caused by API-key shadowing in proxy rotation
creator: Aisha Gupta
description:
Summary: Multiple customers reported over-quota errors followed by delayed billing reconciliation (hours later) after we rotated upstream API keys through the proxy fleet. Root cause appears to be an interaction between API-key shadowing in the edge proxy (short overlap window during rolling rotations), our realtime usage-aggregator that attributes tokens by key, and a separate background reconciliation job that deduplicates and attributes late-arriving proxy logs.

Scope & systems: attribution-service (real-time attribution), proxy (edge key routing + shadowing), usage-aggregator (stream consumer), backfill/reconciliation worker (batch consumer). Affected customers: enterprise accounts with sub-orgs that use short-lived API key rotation and route via our HTTP proxy layer (Dedicated + Private customers behind regional proxies).

Hypothesis: During a rolling key rotation where proxies shadow both old and new key headers for a brief period, some requests are forwarded with the new key but contain the old key in downstream X-Forwarded-Key headers (or vice versa). The realtime attribution uses the first-seen key header from proxy metadata, while the reconciliation job groups by token hash and then applies the latest binding timestamp. A race causes events to be temporarily recorded under an ephemeral placeholder tenant in the realtime store; reconciliation merges them later, creating a delayed reconciliation window which results in incorrect per-project quota enforcement (rate limiter hits) during the interim.

Reproduction steps (local cluster):
1) Create two API keys for workspace W, rotate with overlap enabled on proxies.
2) Send 500 short requests at T0 using new key but with proxy injecting old-key in X-Forwarded-Key for subset of requests.
3) Observe realtime attribution stream showing ~25% of tokens attributed to orphan placeholder id; rate-limiter for project triggers at T0+10s.
4) Run backfill worker manually; observe tokens merged into proper workspace and quota counters corrected.

Initial metrics observed (Prod region us-east-1):
- 2026-02-09 14:03–14:12: abnormal 1.9x increase in "orphan-token" counts per minute for 3 tenants.
- Average reconciliation lag for affected shards: 34 minutes (tail 95th: 2.1 hours).

Immediate mitigation: added an emergency retry in proxy to prefer canonical api_key header and strip stale forwarded key headers when rotation header present. This reduced orphan creation but is tactical.

Long-term fixes considered: 1) make attribution idempotent by token hash + deterministic key binding precedence using rotation-timestamp; 2) change reconciliation worker to fast-path merge for recent windows (<1h) and update rate-limiter to consult both realtime store and reconciliation delta when evaluating per-request quota enforcement.

Notes: this ticket focuses on implementing deterministic attribution precedence and guardrails in rate-limiter evaluation. Separate follow-up will harden proxy rotation choreography and add e2e tests.

acceptance_criteria: Deterministic attribution logic implemented: attribution-service selects binding by token hash and key_binding_timestamp <= request_time
Rate-limiter evaluation consults reconciliation delta for last 10 minutes to avoid premature quota blocks
Backfill/migration completes for >90% shards within maintenance window and decreases reconciliation lag under 10 minutes
E2E tests added that simulate proxy overlap window pass consistently in CI
No increase in end-to-end request latency >2% in canary rolling deployment
mitigation: Short-term: proxy header canonicalization and header-stripping patch deployed to edge on Feb 16 (region us-east-1). Medium-term: deterministic attribution + fast-path reconciliation. Support runbook added to respond to quota complaints: temporarily lift per-project hard limits and force backfill on affected shards.
implementation_notes: Add key_binding_timestamp column (nullable) to attribution DB (migration path: populate from rotation events stream).
Attribution selection algorithm: prefer binding where binding.timestamp <= request_time and has the longest lifetime; fall back to legacy behavior only if no binding exists.
Rate-limiter change: when evaluating a request, consult recent reconciliation-delta cache for token hashes seen in last 10min; merge counters before enforcing hard limits.
Backfill job: implement parallel shard workers with progress checkpoints and idempotent writes; provide opt-in dry-run flag.
Monitoring: add reconciliation-lag metric per-shard and broken-down by workspace. Alert if median > 15m or 95th > 2h.
